defense_analyst.prose:
DET's defense generates steady pressure: it sends five or more rushers on 27.3% of dropbacks [dc1] over 429 plays [dc2], averaging 4.3 rushers per dropback [dc3]. The pressure proxy (sacks plus QB hits) is 17.5% [dc4], and the sack rate of 8.4% [dc5] ranks 4th in the league [dc6]. Expect a fifth rusher on a large share of snaps, so CHI's protection slides and hot-route answers need to be set before the snap. The data here does not split pressure by down, so treat third-down pressure as unverified.

The pass defense is the soft spot. DET allows explosive pass plays on 8.9% of attempts [dc7] and an EPA of 0.10 per pass play [dc8], both costly. Against the run it is stronger, at -0.06 EPA per play [dc9], though explosives still come on 9.8% of carries [dc10] over 204 runs [dc11]. CHI should attack the pass when the rush stays at four and use the run to set up play action.

On third down DET allows conversions on 44.8% of attempts [dc12] over 134 plays [dc13], close to CHI's own 45.0% conversion rate [dc14] over 140 plays [dc15]. In the red zone DET allows touchdowns on 67.6% of drives [dc16] over 34 drives [dc17], while CHI scores touchdowns on 57.5% of its red-zone drives [dc18] over 40 drives [dc19]. Both red-zone samples are small, but red-zone efficiency could decide this game.
